items.body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

AI TUI tools (Kiro CLI, Claude Code, GSD, and similar) render responses inside column-constrained panels and soft-wrap lines at the render width. When those wrapped lines appear in Warp's block output, URLs that span the wrap boundary are split across two rows. Warp's link detector sees only the first fragment as a URL candidate — CMD+click opens the truncated URL, silently failing any auth flow or navigation that depends on it.

**Concrete example** — kiro-cli wraps at its panel width:

```
# Block output as Warp receives it:
Authenticate here: https://auth.example.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=myapp&sta
te=abc123&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmyapp.example.com%2Fcallback
```

Hovering the first line highlights `https://auth.example.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=myapp&sta` as the URL. CMD+click opens that truncated address — the browser reports an invalid request or silently fails the auth flow. The second line (`te=abc123&redirect_uri=...`) is not recognized as a URL at all.

**Second manifestation — interactive Ctrl+y prompt:**

Kiro CLI also presents OAuth URLs via an in-TUI prompt (`Ctrl+y to copy URL`). The URL displayed there is similarly soft-wrapped; `Ctrl+y` copies only the visible fragment to clipboard. The destination URL is inaccessible.

### Root cause

This is a **tokenizer-layer** problem in block output link detection, distinct from but related to the resolution-layer bug in #9908.

Warp's `possible_file_paths_at_point` / `scan_for_file_path` pipeline in `link_detection.rs` processes rows of block output independently. When a URL has been soft-wrapped by an upstream TUI renderer, each row is a valid string — the first fragment passes as a (truncated) URL, the second looks like a bare word. There is no cross-row context to signal that they are halves of the same URL.

The upstream cause is that tools like Kiro CLI copy the rendered terminal buffer rather than raw message text, and do not emit URLs via **OSC 8** (terminal hyperlinks, `\x1b]8;;URI\x07display\x1b]8;;\x07`). If they did, the URI param in the OSC 8 sequence is never soft-wrapped and Warp's click handler could use it directly once #6541 lands. Until then, Warp sees only the wrapped display text.

### Relationship to other issues

This is in the same link-detection subsystem as several related issues — all share `link_detection.rs` / `grid_handler.rs` as the fix site, but address different stages:

| Issue | Stage | Problem | Status |
|-------|-------|---------|--------|
| **#9908** | Resolution | Correct token, wrong resolution root (`ls DIR/`) | PR #10579 in review |
| **#9909** / **#10004** | Tokenizer | Box-drawing chars not in `FILE_LINK_SEPARATORS` | ✅ Fixed in #10004 |
| **This issue** | Tokenizer | Soft-wrapped URL split across rows | Open |
| **#6541** | Renderer | OSC 8 hyperlinks not rendered as clickable | Open — upstream fix |

**This issue is complementary to, not a duplicate of, #11608** (paste_transform). That issue covers the *paste* path — cleaning up artifacts when content is Cmd+V'd into the input block. This issue covers the *click* path — what happens when a user hovers and CMD+clicks a URL in block output. Different code paths; both need fixing independently.

### Expected behavior

1. When a block output row ends with a URL that extends to the end of the line (`https?://\S+$`), and the immediately following row begins with a URL-safe fragment containing URL-specific characters (digits, `%`, `?`, `&`, `=`, `/` — distinguishing real URL tails from prose words), the two rows should be joined into a single URL candidate before link validation.
2. Joined URLs must be clickable and must open the full, reconstructed URL.
3. Behavior is additive — rows that don't match the URL-continuation heuristic are unaffected. Non-URL clickable detection (file paths, per #9908) is unaffected.
4. If #6541 (OSC 8 rendering) lands, OSC 8 URIs should take precedence over this heuristic — the URI param is authoritative and never wrapped.

### Proposed fix

In `possible_file_paths_at_point` or the row-scanning loop that feeds it, before emitting URL candidates, apply a URL-fragment join pass:

```
for each row i in block output:
    if row[i] matches `https?://\S+$`:          // URL reaches end-of-line
        if row[i+1] starts with a URL-continuation fragment:
            //   - no leading whitespace on the fragment
            //   - first token is all URL-safe chars (RFC 3986)
            //   - first token contains at least one of: digit, %, ?, &, =, /
            //     (distinguishes "6085010" from prose words like "for")
            join row[i] + row[i+1].first_token as single URL candidate
            emit remainder of row[i+1] as separate non-URL content
```

The `_is_url_continuation` logic in [tui-clean](https://github.com/rndjams/tui-clean) (MIT) has a tested Python reference implementation for the heuristic and edge cases, including false-positive guards.

**Known limitation:** The heuristic cannot perfectly distinguish a URL continuation from a lowercase prose word that happens to contain URL-safe characters. This is an inherent constraint of heuristic text analysis. The clean fix is OSC 8 (#6541): once kiro-cli and similar tools emit proper hyperlinks, Warp can use the URI param as the authoritative click target regardless of how the display text was wrapped.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Simulate kiro-cli wrapped URL output (any AI TUI tool with long auth URLs)
# Start a kiro-cli chat session, trigger an OAuth authentication URL (e.g.
# connect a GitHub MCP server), observe the URL wraps at the panel width.
# Hover the URL in block output — only the first fragment highlights.
# CMD+click — browser opens the truncated URL (invalid request).
```

For a minimal synthetic test without kiro-cli:

```bash
printf 'Authenticate: https://auth.example.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=myapp&sta\nte=abc123&redirect_uri=https%%3A%%2F%%2Fmyapp.example.com%%2Fcallback\n'
```

Paste this into a Warp block (via `echo` or similar). Hover the first line — only the fragment is highlighted.

### Environment

- macOS 26.4.1 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64)
- zsh 5.9
- Warp v0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable_03
- Reproducible with: Kiro CLI 2.4.x (default TUI mode), Claude Code, GSD

### Additional context

**Upstream tracking:** kiro-cli filed as [kirodotdev/Kiro#8814](https://github.com/kirodotdev/Kiro/issues/8814) — root cause is that `/copy to clipboard` and TUI rendering scrape the rendered buffer rather than using OSC 52 / OSC 8.

**Workaround (paste path only):** [tui-clean](https://github.com/rndjams/tui-clean) rejoins URL fragments when pasting via the ZLE bracketed-paste hook. Does not help with block-output clicks; that requires a Warp-side fix.

**Scope boundary:** This issue covers single-line URL wraps. Multi-line URLs (where the URL wraps more than once) are out of scope for V1 — they're rare and the fix is iterative.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes — other terminals don't have clickable link detection in block output, so the problem manifests differently (no click at all vs. wrong click).

items.body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Cloud-synced agent conversations inconsistently fail to appear in the conversation list (`/conversations`), even though cloud conversation sync is enabled on a paid plan. Additionally, `Ctrl+Shift+H` (toggle conversation list panel) does not respond on Linux.

## Problem
With "Store AI conversations in the cloud" enabled in Settings > Privacy, local agent conversations are not reliably persisted and surfaced in the conversation list. The user had a conversation this morning that does not appear in `/conversations` at all. The conversation list shows conversations from up to 5 months ago but is missing the most recent one. This has happened inconsistently across multiple occasions.

Separately, the `Ctrl+Shift+H` shortcut (documented as "Toggle conversation list panel" on Linux) produces no response.

## Expected behavior
1. All local agent conversations should appear in `/conversations` after a Warp restart, especially with cloud sync enabled on a paid plan.
2. `Ctrl+Shift+H` should toggle the conversation list panel on Linux.

## Actual behavior
1. Recent conversations intermittently disappear from the conversation list after restarting Warp. The conversation from this morning is completely absent despite older conversations (up to 5 months old) being present.
2. `Ctrl+Shift+H` does nothing.

## Reproduction steps
1. Enable "Store AI conversations in the cloud" in Settings > Privacy (paid plan).
2. Have a local agent conversation in Warp.
3. Restart Warp.
4. Type `/conversations` to open the conversation list.
5. Observe that the recent conversation is missing from the list.
6. Press `Ctrl+Shift+H` — nothing happens.

## Artifacts
None attached.

## Warp version
v0.2026.05.13.09.15.stable_03

## Operating system
Fedora Linux 43

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

I contacted support and they suggested opening a ticket.

Warp does not allow you to see what the agent said in warpified sessions, only what it did unlike local sessions where it is shown in line.

Once it is done with everything you have no idea what suggestions or things to do next that it said. 

Ideally there is a way to pull back this chat history between you in the client in a ssh warpified session.

Here is what support said:

From the information available, Warp’s “session history” and conversation search (via CMD+Y on macOS or CTRL+SHIFT+Y on Windows/Linux) only apply to local Agent conversations, and that history is stored locally and flushed when you log out of Warp. [Session history; Agent conversations]

The knowledge sources do not mention any way to:
Persist or replay the full, step‑by‑step interactive output from a Warpified SSH session, or
Have that SSH interaction appear in the Agent conversation history/search.
In other words, what Warp told you (“the interactive content from Warp's SSH sessions isn't saved to the chat history”) matches what’s documented; I don’t see any hidden setting or workaround in the docs that would expose that output after it has scrolled away.

Given this, the only reliable way (based on current docs) to keep that information is to manually copy it while it’s visible (e.g., select and copy, or pipe commands to a log file on the remote machine). The docs do not describe any built‑in “scrollback replay” or automatic logging for Warpified SSH sessions. [SSH Warpify; SSH Legacy]

### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Workflows are great for static commands, however, there is currently no way for the terminal UI to dynamically adapt to a "Call to Action" (CTA) within the terminal output. 

### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like Warp to implement a **Contextual Action Layer** that bridges the gap between a CLI and a GUI. This includes two main components:

#### 1. Dynamic Response Buttons (Agentic Interaction)
When a terminal process or Warp AI asks a question (e.g., *"Would you like me to proceed with x, y, z?"*), Warp should allow for the injection of temporary, keybound buttons alongside the standard block actions.
* **Example UI:** Instead of just "Hide Response," the block header could display:
    `[Yes to All (Ctrl+Shift+A)] [Option X (Ctrl+1)] [Option Y (Ctrl+2)]`
* **Input Types:** Support for Radio buttons or Checkboxes within a block to select multiple parameters before hitting a "Submit" or "Run" button.

#### 2. Pre-programmed Contextual Buttons (Heuristic UI)
A feature that allows users to define "Context Rules" that trigger specific GUI buttons.
* **Trigger:** If the terminal output matches a regex or if the user is in a specific directory/git branch.
* **Action:** A custom button appears in the Warp UI that, when clicked (or triggered via keybinding), executes a pre-defined prompt or command.
* **Auto-Detection:** Warp could track frequently used commands in specific contexts and suggest these as "Quick Action" buttons to reduce repetitive typing.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
* **Workflows:** These require manual searching and don't "surface" themselves based on output context.
* **Alias/Scripts:** These still require manual typing and don't provide the visual "state" (like checkboxes) that a GUI does.

### Additional context
This would essentially turn Warp into a "Low-Code" terminal environment where the output can dictate the most likely next inputs, significantly increasing velocity for DevOps and development workflows.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I find myself repeatedly typing the same confirmation commands or selecting the same options when interacting with CLI tools, scripts, or Warp AI agents. 

### Additional context

I think this would make Warp stand further apart from the competitor GUI based terminals by modernizing the Call To Action component of interacting with an Agentic Terminal. The goal of the project is to make life in the terminal easier and I believe this would provide something unique and powerful for the community to run away with. 

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### How important is this feature to you?

4

items.body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [x] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

On Windows, after an unclean shutdown (e.g., power loss) during a large, multi‑agent session, relaunching Warp produces a process that is alive and pumping the Windows message loop (Task Manager shows Responding) but is functionally frozen — the UI never becomes interactive, agents never resume, the process pins ~8 GB RAM, and it cannot be closed cleanly (requires force‑termination). Launching Warp again starts a second full instance that fails to bind the single‑instance port 127.0.0.1:9277.

A full user‑mode dump (cdb/WinDbg) shows all 123 threads parked idle — 78 in ntdll!NtWaitForAlertByThreadId, 31 in NtWaitForSingleObject, plus message‑pump/IOCP threads — with no OS‑level deadlock: !locks found 0 of 23 critical sections contended, no SRW/critical‑section waits, no synchronous file/socket I/O, and no network‑stack frames. !analyze -v -hang reports APPLICATION_HANG_..._win32u.dll!NtUserMsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx (UI thread in the normal idle message wait). This indicates a logical async‑runtime stall (background work that never gets scheduled/woken), not a mutex deadlock or blocked syscall.

The pre‑freeze log backtrace runs through onig_get_string_by_callout_args → git_index_checksum (Tree‑sitter/Oniguruma + Git indexing), so this looks like the quiesced/stalled phase of the runaway Git‑indexing/Tree‑sitter executor in #8545 (same machine — #8545 was caught mid‑runaway with unbounded memory/disk; this one caught after it stalled). The database is intact: PRAGMA quick_check on a copy of warp.sqlite returned ok.

### To reproduce

1. Use Warp on Windows with a large, long-running multi-agent session (the local DB grows large — here warp.sqlite ≈ 3.3 GB, agent_tasks ≈ 2.6 GB, thousands of AI blocks).
2. While Warp is running, trigger an unclean shutdown (power loss / forced power-off) so it does not exit cleanly (SQLite WAL left dirty).
3. Power back on and launch Warp. On startup it performs WAL recovery (SQLite error 283 ... recovered 145 frames from WAL).
4. The relaunched instance hangs: the window reports "Responding" but never becomes interactive, agents don't resume, ~8 GB RAM stays pinned, and it can't be closed cleanly.
5. Launch Warp again → a second instance starts and logs: Failed to bind local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1:9277 ... (os error 10048).

Frequency: intermittent but recurring — after power loss, and sometimes after ordinary reboots; correlates with large session/restore size.

### Expected behavior

After an unclean shutdown, Warp should either fully recover the session and become interactive, or fail fast with a clear error. Background workers (Git indexing / syntax parsing) should throttle or terminate and release memory, and Warp should exit cleanly even if they can't quiesce. Relaunching should focus the existing instance rather than starting a second one that can't bind 9277.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Relevant warp.log* lines around the failed startup:
•  SQLite error 283 (A WAL mode database file was recovered): recovered 145 frames from WAL file ...\warp.sqlite-wal
•  Failed to bind local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1:9277: Only one usage of each socket address ... (os error 10048)
•  IPC server disconnected unexpectedly
•  Received 'end_in_band_command_output' while not expecting to read in-band command output.

Artifacts captured locally (available on request — the dump is too large to attach):
•  Full user‑mode dump warp_38844.dmp (~9.6 GB)
•  cdb analysis.log (all 123 thread stacks, !analyze -v -hang, !locks)
•  Open‑handle snapshot; verified warp.sqlite backup (quick_check = ok)

Full diagnostics (including the complete analysis.log) were also posted on the earlier report #12793. Log location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\logs\warp.log*

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### Operating system and version

10.0.26200

### Shell Version

PowerShell 7.5.5 (pwsh)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.06.10.09.27.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

•  Same root cause as #8545 (bug, triaged, ready-to-implement) — this is the quiesced/stalled phase of that runaway Git‑indexing/Tree‑sitter executor, with a power‑loss trigger and the dual‑instance / port‑9277 symptom.
•  This re‑files #12793 using the official Bug Report template. #12793 contains the full diagnostics, but its automated triage (oz-for-oss / triage-new-issues, run_id 019edbc8-bc98-7bd5-831a-d1fd6051152e) errored and never completed, so it was never labeled/assigned. Happy to close #12793 as superseded by this issue.
•  Not AI‑related (no debugging ID). Windows‑only; not Linux, so X11/Wayland and eglinfo are N/A.
•  A validated recovery is documented (back up the warp.sqlite + -wal + -shm triplet, then end the stuck PID; the port frees and one fresh instance restores normally).

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

### Warp Internal (ignore): linear-label:b9d78064-c89e-4973-b153-5178a31ee54e

_No response_

### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Allow user to Save Sessions and access them via Sesson History 


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, Warp saves the data from your previous session's windows, tabs, and panes to a SQLite database on your computer, and every time you quit the app, this **data is overwritten by your latest session**

This feature will remove the overwrite functionality and replace it with an historical, Session History list so users can easily recall previous sessions and context. Allow user to name session or save with date/time for easy access from Session History.

### Additional context

Currently, if users close a session tab the session is lost (overwritten) if the application is closed for any reason. As a workaround, the user has to save and manually organize conversations and then cut/paste into a new tab to restore some context but is error prone and laborious. This new feature makes it easy to pick-up previously closed tabs/sessions with full conversations and context persisted. Importantly, this prevents accidental loss of work as reported by many users.

### Discord username (optional)

### Describe the bug

Generally speaking, the Copy On Select feature works fine for me in most areas of Warp. However, when I use vim (`VIM - Vi IMproved 9.0 (2022 Jun 28, compiled Dec 16 2022 23:27:53)`) or any other program that runs a whole TUI (`less`, `screen`, `gdb`'s tui, the default terminal paging for `git log`), I find that Copy On Select doesn't work at all on my local machine (selecting works fine, but whatever I select is not added to the paste buffer; it is only possible to copy with Cmd+C).

### To Reproduce

1. Open a program that runs in a TUI
2. Highlight a line of text
3. Use cmd+v to paste; it will not paste the highlighted text.

### Expected behaviour

I expect that when Copy On Select is enabled, selecting text in Warp will result in that text being added to the paste buffer, even in vim (and other applications with paging).

### Screenshots

https://github.com/warpdotdev/Warp/assets/4369667/8dc2fb5e-4020-4a9c-b39f-07df0dffcc2e

MacOS

13.2.1 (and all other current macOS versions through 14.4)

zsh 5.8.1 (via oh-my-zsh) (also seen in zsh 5.9)

v0.2023.03.07.08.02.stable_01 (still seen in every version up to and including v0.2024.02.20.08.01.stable_02)

### Additional context

I'm not blocked from using Warp daily because of this, but it's pretty annoying unexpected behavior (not least because generally one doesn't want text from the paste buffer to end up getting pasted in an unintended context! consequences could range from innocuous to embarrassing all the way to full-blown incorrect input / security issue).
